problem.title: Two Sum
problem.statement: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target. Each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice. Return the indices in any order.
problem.constraints: 2 <= nums.length <= 10^4; -10^9 <= nums[i], target <= 10^9; exactly one valid answer exists.

events.text: Array up to 10^4 ints, values can be negative, exactly one answer, can't reuse an element. What's the cleanest approach?
Two options: nested loops in O(n^2), or a hash map of seen values in O(n). Insert each number into the map first, then look up target - x. Order doesn't matter here.
That can't be right: with [3,2,4] and target 6, inserting 3 first then finding 3 returns [0,0], the same element twice.
You're right, that was wrong. Thanks for the counterexample; use the corrected condition.
Before I code it: what edge cases should I handle, like duplicates or negatives?
Those cover it. Your counterexample is a good test to keep.
